text:
Jason: Alert — we're seeing ~50% auth failures and console timeouts in west1. Errors coming from auth-proxy and controlplane API gateway.

sre-bot: [ALERT] controlplane.auth_proxy.errors > 30% for 5m — incident opened. Link: https://internal/alerts/2083456789 :rotating_light:

Anika: ack — looking. Can someone grab netstat/conntrack stats from the egress NAT stack?

Raj: pulling from west1-nat-01 now. quick output: ```conntrack: entries=65536 used=65536 found=0```.

Oliver: confirmed on west1-egress LB hosts — kernel logs show `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` and lots of TCP_SYN_RECV timeouts.

Maria: that will cause auth token handshakes to fail (short-lived connections). If we don't fix quickly console will stay flaky.

Anika: ops-bot, any recent rollout that increased connection churn?

ops-bot: Recent rollout: controlplane-proxy v2.14 -> v2.15 pushed 2h ago to west1 (canary). No rollback yet. Autoscaler scaled proxy pool +40% in last 30m.

Jason: might be combined effect: proxy counts up, conntrack not tuned, and upstream LB hit limit. We should avoid rollback if possible; prefer increasing conntrack and scaling NAT.

Raj: proposing immediate mitigation: bump nf_conntrack_max on egress hosts and increase conntrack hashsize. Commands: ```sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_hashsize=32768```

Oliver: rolling sysctl change across hosts now via runbook (small risk: increased memory usage on NAT hosts). Doing 3 hosts at a time.

Anika: also put controlplane routing into fallback mode so we can drain sessions off west1 to na-east1 for control traffic only. Maria, can you coordinate traffic shift for control plane? :eyes:

Maria: starting control-plane-only traffic shift to na-east1 (no compute workloads yet). Will ramp 10% -> 50% over 15m and monitor auth error rate.

Raj: note: shifting control traffic will increase cross-region egress charges and may temporarily saturate na-east1 NATs — plan to stand up 2 extra egress VMs there (onspot) for 30m.

Jason: do it. Cost > outage. Add cost note to incident timeline.

sre-bot: action created: SRE-5267 increase-conntrack-west1 (assigned: Raj) — ETA 10m.

Oliver: conntrack bump completed on west1-nat-0[1-3]. immediate drop in drops. auth error rate falling: from 48% -> 12% in 5m.

Anika: nice. Keep monitoring. Maria, how's routing shift?

Maria: 30% shifted now; auth failures down to ~6%, console latencies improving. Some controlplane components still showing leader-election flapping — likely due to earlier token churn. Rolling back any config rollouts until cluster stable.

Jason: freeze config rollouts in west1 and mark etcd leader under observation. Anika, set rollout freeze in the console and add message to oncall-runbook.

Anika: done — rollout freeze applied, console now shows read-only banner for west1 controllers.

Raj: will follow up with kernel tuning PR to persist conntrack changes and add autoscale hook for conntrack usage. Ticket SRE-5268 created.

Oliver: added temporary autoscaler policy on west1-proxy to limit burst scale to avoid re-exhausting conntrack while we deploy persistent fix.

Jason: declaring Sev2 incident. Summary for postmortem: root cause = NAT conntrack table exhaustion combined with a recent proxy scaleup; cascade caused controlplane auth failures and console timeouts. Mitigations: conntrack bump, traffic shift, rollout freeze, autoscaler throttle.

Maria: I'll draft a customer-facing note and cost estimate for cross-region egress. Expect draft in 30m.

sre-bot: incident updated to SEV2 — timeline and actions logged.

Anika: next steps: (1) persist sysctl via image/ansible, (2) add conntrack metrics to autoscaler triggers, (3) postmortem and cost breakdown. Assign owners?

Jason: owners: Raj (conntrack persist + metrics), Oliver (autoscaler policy + rollout), Maria (customer comms + cost), Anika (postmortem). Closing temporary actions once error rate <1% for 30m. :white_check_mark:
